messages.text: Our dad died and left the house in his will. My sister A wants to buy it with her husband at a "family discount". I'm not signing off on that. Our younger sister B could use some money too. Can you help us sort this out?
I want a fair financial share of the house’s value. I haven’t agreed to a discounted purchase, and I’m not in a rush to settle it.

I’d like to buy the house with my husband at a family discount, so we can make it our home. I’m open to discussing other options, but I can’t commit without understanding the proposed value and shares. I know C hasn’t agreed.

Thank you. I’d like my share of the house’s value to help me start a dance studio. If it’s possible to settle that sooner rather than later, that would help, though I understand the value and timing still need to be worked out.

**Updated list**
1. C will not sign off on A buying the house with her husband at a family discount.
2. C wants a fair financial share of the house’s value and is not in a rush to settle.
3. B would like money from her share to start a dance studio, preferably without undue delay.

I can’t name a fair price yet; I’d want an independent valuation and clarity on everyone’s shares first. My husband and I would need to work out financing against that figure, and I can’t promise what we could pay.
B can be paid sooner; I don’t need the same timetable. But my fair share must be valued and protected, and I can’t agree to specifics before we know the proposed price and shares.
That sounds reasonable. I’m willing to get an independent valuation and have the will’s terms clarified before we discuss a purchase price.
That makes sense. I agree an independent valuation is a sensible next step, but I haven’t agreed to a discounted sale or any payment terms.
Yes, that seems sensible. I can wait until the will’s terms and the independent valuation are clear, though I’d appreciate working toward payment as soon as those are settled.
That covers my concern. I’d just like us to keep working toward my payment as soon as the will and valuation allow.
That reflects my position. I agree only to clarifying the will and getting an independent valuation; no sale price, discount, or payment terms are agreed.
That captures my concern. I agree the first two steps are to clarify the will and get an independent valuation; I can’t commit to a purchase until we know the shares and work out financing.
